newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World Jewish Congress official in Berne for talks.
newsitem.headline: World Jewish Congress official in Berne for talks.

text.p: Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti was due to meet a senior official of the World Jewsih Congress (WJC) on Monday, two weeks after Berne and major Jewish groups agreed to cooperate in compensating Holocaust victims.

WJC secretary general Israel Singer was to meet Cotti and other Swiss leaders on Monday and Tuesday to discuss what Switzerland had done so far and its future plans for redressing what critics call cynically profitting from World War Two.

Singer said the WJC, which for months had hammered the Swiss with critcism, now wanted to cooperate after Swiss banks and the government agreed to set up a humanitarian fund for Holocaust survivors as well as probe the country's financial role in World War Two.
"There are no problems. We have engaged ourselves in a process and we trust and hope this process will bear fruit and continue to develop and grow," he told Swiss radio.

Jewish groups led by the WJC had demanded the rapid creation of a humanitarian fund so that ageing Holocaust survivors could be helped before the long process of tracking Jewish accounts and Nazi loot through Swiss banks, which could take until mid-1998 at least.

The Swiss government, which at the start of the year said it would never establish such a fund, announced two weeks ago that it would take over a private 100 million Swiss franc ($69 million) set up by the country's three biggest banks and work with the WJC and Swiss Jews to set up a mechanism for its "timely distribution".

Details of how the fund will be set up and exactly how it would benefit Holocaust survivors are being negotiated now between the Swiss and Jewish sides and are likely to be a part of Singer's meetings.

Sources close to the negotiations have said they expect a foundation to be set up to administer payments and give priority to the neediest survivors and those who never received any compensation, like the Jews of Eastern Europe.
